concepts.name: Cluster Provisioning (dev on Hetzner)
concepts.summary: Declarative k3s cluster (oriso-dev, k3s v1.32.0+k3s1, Nuremberg/nbg1) on Hetzner Cloud via the hetzner-k3s CLI: clusters/dev-hetzner/cluster.yaml defines 1 CX23 control-plane node plus an autoscaling CX33 worker pool (2-5 nodes), flannel CNI, private network 10.0.0.0/16, metrics-server and Spegel embedded registry mirror enabled, Traefik and ServiceLB explicitly disabled. apply.sh is the one-command provision+bootstrap entrypoint; hetzner-k3s must run from the cluster directory so kubeconfig lands next to cluster.yaml. Staging/prod run on Gridscale GSK and are managed separately.

concepts.name: In-Cluster Bootstrap
concepts.summary: bootstrap/bootstrap.sh idempotently installs the minimal cluster-level baseline the ORISO platform chart expects to pre-exist: cert-manager (pinned v1.16.2, Helm values under bootstrap/values/ with CRDs installed and kept), the caritas application namespace, and the block-storage StorageClass. Post-bootstrap manual steps (documented in bootstrap/README.md): create the GHCR registry-secret in caritas and install the ORISO platform chart with a local gitignored values-dev.yaml.

concepts.name: Block Storage StorageClass Alias
concepts.summary: StorageClass block-storage is a pure alias for Hetzner CSI's hcloud-volumes (provisioner csi.hetzner.cloud, WaitForFirstConsumer, reclaim Delete, expansion allowed) so the ORISO chart's storageClassName: block-storage references (Matrix Synapse data/media/postgres PVCs) work without chart changes. Persistent data lives on Hetzner Volumes, not on node disks.

concepts.name: Developer Access Management
concepts.summary: Per-developer cluster access via personal ServiceAccounts: add-developer.sh creates ServiceAccount dev-<user>, a namespace-scoped RoleBinding to the built-in admin ClusterRole in caritas, and a long-lived token Secret (all labelled oriso.io/user=<name>), then emits a personal kubeconfig for secure one-time hand-off. Developers get full rights inside caritas but no cluster-level or cross-namespace access. remove-developer.sh deletes everything by label, invalidating the kubeconfig immediately. ACCESS-MANAGEMENT.md documents both the admin and developer procedures.

concepts.name: Network Exposure & Firewall Allowlists
concepts.summary: Hetzner Cloud Firewall allowlists are declared in cluster.yaml: both the Kubernetes API server and SSH are currently open to 0.0.0.0/0 (auth relies on mTLS admin kubeconfig and ServiceAccount tokens). The stated long-term plan is to move both behind a Tailscale mesh VPN (CGNAT range). Note ACCESS-MANAGEMENT.md still describes SSH as firewalled to the admin's IP, which no longer matches cluster.yaml.

flows.name: Provision & Bootstrap Cluster
flows.summary: export HCLOUD_TOKEN, then apply.sh: Phase 1 cd's into clusters/dev-hetzner and runs hetzner-k3s create against cluster.yaml (network, firewall, VMs, LB, k3s, Hetzner CCM/CSI, Spegel; kubeconfig written locally, gitignored) → Phase 2 runs bootstrap/bootstrap.sh (cert-manager, caritas namespace, block-storage StorageClass) → operator manually creates the GHCR registry-secret and installs the ORISO platform chart into caritas. Re-running is safe; hetzner-k3s applies only the diff.

flows.name: Developer On/Offboarding
flows.summary: Admin points KUBECONFIG at the admin kubeconfig and runs add-developer.sh <username> (DNS-friendly name) → script applies SA + RoleBinding + token Secret in caritas, waits for the token controller, and writes <username>-kubeconfig.yaml (mode 600) → admin hands the file over via a secure one-time channel and deletes the local copy → developer saves it as ~/.kube/oriso-dev. Offboarding: remove-developer.sh <username> deletes all resources by the oriso.io/user label.
